Subject: Accelerator cohort — hardware needs + promo support?

Hi Mina —

Thanks again for the product walkthrough yesterday. We’re finalizing the curriculum for our summer accelerator cohort (EdgeWorks Batch 9) and wanted to check whether Redwood has an existing path for startups that need sustained GPU/TPU-heavy inference during a 12-week pilot. A couple of details:

- Typical cohort apps will do scheduled inference runs (10–15k tokens/day app average) but a subset (3 teams) will run near real-time inference with long seq lengths (up to 8k tokens) and periodic batch training steps.
- We’re evaluating a sponsor model where we cover base usage and ask Redwood for free credits or an elevated free tier for those three teams while they’re in-program.
- Budget for the sponsor line is limited — we need clarity on packaging, any eligible promo credit caps, and whether a temporary dedicated pool is required.

Attached is a short spec doc (EdgeWorks_ACC_Tier_Specs.pdf) that lists expected consumption patterns. Can you share what flexibility you have for accelerator/promotional credits and whether Redwood would consider a short-term waiver to the standard promo limits for hardware-heavy cohorts?

If it helps, we can do a 30-minute call with your partnerships team later this week.

Best,
Sara

Hi Sara —

Appreciate the spec and the context — this is the kind of use case we love to support. Quick notes:

- Promo credit policy: our standard accelerator credit package covers up to $10k in credits per cohort team for 12 weeks. For GPU/long-seq workloads we typically recommend Dedicated pools or a higher-cap hosted allocation to keep latencies stable.
- Waiver path: we do have a discretionary waiver channel for sponsored cohorts, but approvals are done on a case-by-case basis and require: (1) expected consumption profile, (2) a mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones, and (3) a short-term cap + overage plan.
- Timing: if you can confirm the three teams and share an expected peak QPS and monthly token estimate we can run a quick cost model and scope a one-off promo top-up.

I’m looping in Ben (partnerships lead) and Lauren (pricing ops) to help scope and document a MAP. Would you be available tomorrow at 10am PT for a 30-minute sync?

Thanks —
Mina
Mina Haddad

Thanks for the summary — I reviewed the MAP and the ask. Decision: approve a one-time cohort promo top-up of $25,000 (applied to the cohort pool) as a discretionary marketing/sales credit, subject to the following:

1) Include a five-item acceptance checklist in the MAP: participant list, expected peak QPS, sample workload, signed mutual action plan, and a program post-mortem within 30 days of cohort end.
2) Set a hard cap: the $25k covers up to the specified 6-week heavy inference window; any material overage moves to the discounted overage rate in the MAP.
3) Require a countersigned agreement via DocuSign with the MAP and a short SOW clause (we’ll use the standard promo waiver addendum).

Ben — please prepare the external-facing MAP and the DocuSign envelope. Mina — please own the external communications and ensure the cohort list + workload samples arrive before launching the dedicated pool. Lauren — confirm the billing code and discount rate for overages.

Marissa Cole
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference
